answer:
**A sliding window limits how far back each query can look.** Full causal attention considers every earlier token. Windowed attention considers only a recent region, reducing the number of permitted comparisons. This resembles reading with a fixed-size recent context instead of reopening the entire document for every new word. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135)

**Make the boundary concrete.** With a window size of three that includes the current token, query position five can see keys at positions three, four, and five. It cannot see positions zero through two, and causality still forbids positions six onward. The predicate is $0\le i-j<3$. If the window is one, each query sees only itself.

The same logic must hold during cached decoding. If five tokens are already cached, the first new query has absolute position five, not zero. Constructing its mask with a reset position would expose the wrong keys or hide every key. A test with nonzero query offset is therefore essential.

**A mask alone is not a speedup.** If the code first creates the full $S\times S$ score matrix and then sets most entries to negative infinity, it has already paid much of the dense memory/computation cost. A sparse or local kernel must avoid generating the forbidden entries to obtain the intended scaling benefit.

**Understand the modeling tradeoff.** Local attention can work well for nearby dependencies, and multiple layers can carry information farther indirectly. But it is not equivalent to direct access to arbitrary distant tokens. A detail far outside the window may be lost or require a separate global/memory mechanism. Evaluate long-distance tasks explicitly instead of assuming reduced memory leaves model quality unchanged.

**Technical details and references.**

A key is visible when 0 ≤ query_position−key_position < window. This convention includes the current token, so window=1 exposes only self-attention. Absolute offsets make the same predicate work during cached decoding. Creating a dense band mask alone does not reduce quadratic attention work: a local/sparse kernel must exploit the band.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For a window including self, the visibility predicate is $0\le i-j<w$. The number of visible score entries is at most $BSHw$, but a dense implementation can still allocate $BS^2H$ entries. To obtain the intended asymptotic memory/computation benefit, the kernel must skip masked positions rather than merely fill them with negative infinity. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://dev.to/dev48v/sliding-window-attention-a-banded-mask-turns-on2-into-onw-and-stacking-l-layers-buys-an-leg) and [2](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/longformer).
